title: In vitro flow cytometry assay for macrophage phagocytosis of live cells
author: Liu, Mulugeta, et al.

steps.title: Differentiate mouse bone marrow macrophages
steps.instruction: Isolate mouse femurs, flush bone marrow with ice‑cold PBS, filter, centrifuge, lyse red blood cells, count, and plate in RPMI complete with 20 ng/mL recombinant murine M‑CSF for five days, feeding on days 2 and 4.

substeps.instruction: Euthanize mouse by CO₂ asphyxiation, spray abdomen and hind legs with 70 % ethanol, open abdomen, remove skin, cut hind legs above hip and below knee, keep femur joints intact.
Clean muscles from bones with scissors, forceps and Kimwipes; rinse bones once in 70 % ethanol then twice in PBS.
Prepare a 10‑mL syringe with a 27‑gauge needle filled with ice‑cold PBS; cut off bone ends and flush marrow until bones turn translucent, collecting marrow into a sterile dish.
Pipet the marrow up and down with a 10 mL serological pipette and filter through a 40 µm filter into a 50 mL conical tube; centrifuge 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL ACK lysis buffer, leave 30 s, quench with 9 mL PBS, centrifuge 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, count cells with a hemocytometer and aspirate supernatant.

Resuspend cells in RPMI complete medium supplemented with 20 ng/mL recombinant murine M‑CSF at 500 000 cells/mL; plate 10–15 × 10⁶ cells in 20–30 mL per 150 × 15 mm petri dish (≈10–15 million cells per dish).
Incubate plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for five days.
On days 2 and 4, add the same volume of fresh RPMI complete with 20 ng/mL M‑CSF as originally plated; if the dish is too confluent, aspirate half of the previous media before adding fresh media.

steps.title: Differentiate human monocyte macrophages
steps.instruction: Isolate PBMCs from a leukapheresis collar, wash, layer on Ficoll‑Paque, centrifuge, collect buffy coat, wash, count, and plate in RPMI complete with 50 ng/mL recombinant human M‑CSF for five days, feeding on days 2 and 4.

substeps.instruction: Obtain a leukapheresis collar, spray with 70 % ethanol, dry with a Kimwipe, cut both sides and let blood drip into a 50 mL conical tube (≈10 mL per collar).
Mix blood with an equal volume of PBS.
In a second 50 mL tube, add Ficoll‑Paque equal to the original blood volume; gently layer the blood/PBS mixture on top of the Ficoll without mixing.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 30 min at 4 °C using slow acceleration and no brake.
Collect the white buffy coat at the plasma/Ficoll interface, wash in 50 mL PBS, then centrifuge 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

Count cells with a hemocytometer, resuspend in RPMI complete supplemented with 50 ng/mL recombinant human M‑CSF at 500 000 cells/mL; plate 10–15 × 10⁶ cells in 20–30 mL per 150 × 15 mm petri dish (≈1–2 million cells per mL).
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for five days.
On days 2 and 4, add the same volume of fresh RPMI complete with 50 ng/mL M‑CSF as originally plated; if the dish is too confluent, aspirate half of the previous media before adding fresh media.

steps.title: Replate macrophages into 12-well plates
steps.instruction: Detach differentiated macrophages with trypsin, count, and seed 25 000–100 000 cells/mL (aim 100 000 cells per well) into 12‑well plates, allowing ≥8 h attachment before assay.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate supernatant from petri dishes and wash adherent macrophages with 5–10 mL PBS (mouse: one gentle rinse; human: three more forceful rinses).
Add 5 mL trypsin per dish, incubate up to 15 min at 37 °C until cells detach.
Tilt dish at 45°, collect trypsinized cells into a 50 mL conical tube; rinse the dish three times with PBS using a 10 mL serological pipette, adding rinsates to the same tube.
Centrifuge the pooled cells at 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Count cells, resuspend in RPMI complete with the appropriate species‑specific M‑CSF, and dispense 1 mL per well at 25 000–100 000 cells/mL (target 100 000 cells/well).
Rock the plate gently front‑to‑back and side‑to‑side to distribute cells evenly.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for at least 24 h (add fresh RPMI complete with M‑CSF every 2–3 days if not using plates within 2 days).

steps.title: Prepare and label tumor cells
steps.instruction: Harvest tumor cells, wash, trypsinize, quench, perform three PBS washes, optionally stain with CFSE (2 µM, 5 min) or CTV (5 µM, 20 min), and resuspend at the desired concentration in RPMI complete with M‑CSF.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate medium from tumor‑cell flask and wash three times with 10 mL PBS.
Add 1 mL 0.25 % trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 2–3 min at 37 °C, then quench with 9 mL RPMI complete and collect cells into a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant, resuspend in 10 mL HBSS, centrifuge again (400 × g, 5 min, 4 °C) and repeat two more washes (total three washes).
During the second wash, take a small aliquot and count cells with a hemocytometer.

Optional fluorescent labeling: prepare HBSS‑CFSE (2 µM) or HBSS‑CTV (5 µM) in a 37 °C water bath; after the three HBSS washes, resuspend cells at 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL in the dye solution, incubate 5 min (CFSE) or 20 min (CTV) at 37 °C, centrifuge 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate dye solution, and wash three times with ice‑cold HBSS.

steps.title: Plate tumor cells onto macrophages
steps.instruction: Add tumor cells (and optional 2× treatment solutions) to macrophage‑seeded 12‑well plates at a 1:1 ratio, include appropriate controls, and incubate 18–24 h.

substeps.instruction: Determine the volume of tumor‑cell suspension needed so that each well receives the desired number of tumor cells (e.g., 100 000 cells for 100 000 macrophages) in a final volume of 1 mL.
Resuspend tumor cells in RPMI complete with the species‑specific M‑CSF; keep on ice until plating.
If adding treatments (e.g., LCL‑161, IFN‑γ, lymphotoxin), prepare them in RPMI complete with M‑CSF at 2× the final concentration.
Aspirate supernatant from the macrophage plates; optionally wash plates three times with PBS (tilt at 45° and gently aspirate from the side).
For each condition, add either 1 mL of 1× tumor‑cell suspension (no treatment) or 500 µL of 2× tumor‑cell suspension followed by 500 µL of 2× treatment solution.
Include a macrophage‑only well and a tumor‑cell‑only well as negative controls.
Rock the plate gently front‑to‑back and side‑to‑side to distribute cells evenly.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 18–24 h.

steps.title: Harvest and stain cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Collect supernatant and trypsinized cells from each well, centrifuge, stain with anti‑CD45 antibody, fix with 1 % formalin, and store at 4 °C until analysis.

substeps.instruction: Prepare flow‑cytometry tubes containing 2 mL HBSS for each well.
Pipette the 1 mL supernatant from each well into the corresponding tube (collect non‑adherent cells).
Add 1 mL 0.25 % trypsin‑EDTA to each well, incubate 15 min at 37 °C.

Collect the trypsinized cells into the same flow tubes while keeping plates and tubes on ice; tilt plates at 45°, pipette around the well circumference, and verify complete collection under a microscope.
Centrifuge tubes at 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

Prepare stain: for human samples, mix 100 µL FACS buffer with 1 µL anti‑human CD45 antibody per sample (<0.5 × 10⁶ cells); for mouse samples, mix 50 µL FACS buffer with 0.2 µL anti‑mouse CD45 antibody per sample (<0.5 × 10⁶ cells).
Decant supernatant without disturbing pellets, add the appropriate stain, vortex briefly, and incubate 15 min on ice protected from light.
Add 200 µL 1 % formalin to each tube to fix the cells.
Store tubes at 4 °C, protected from light, until flow‑cytometry acquisition.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for assessing primary human and mouse macrophage phagocytosis of live cells.
